facts.claim: Bit depth appears to follow the number of distinct codes in a frame (inferred, not documented)
facts.value: 8-bit frames had up to 169 distinct codes and 16-bit frames as few as 127 (721 frames, 2025-06-25/26). No code-count threshold separates them.

facts.refuted_by: Refuted by 721 frames of 2025-06-25/26: a code-count threshold misses 12 of 73 sampled frames (16-bit at 127 codes; 8-bit at 169 codes). The scaled-range rule fits all 721 frames (new fact).
facts.corrected_from: 8-bit files had 2 to 117 distinct codes (valid values plus present negative codes); 16-bit files had 128 to 345. A 127-code rule would separate all 25 files. Inference only.

limits: Per-file sizes for 2021, 2023 and 2025 come from S3 listings (exact gz bytes as stored). Data was downloaded only for the files named in urls_checked.
Decoding covered 25 distinct 2-minute files, about 15 one-off 1440-minute and 2-minute sample files, and two full 720-frame windows. No 5-year maximum over all 1,826 days was computed.
The 720-frame window test covered the Montana crop (43.0 to 50.5 N, 118.5 to 101.0 W) and the 15 km Benchland disk, on two days only.
Grid-point fractions are not area-weighted; cell area shrinks with latitude across the crop.
Maxima are file values. No point report, storm report or damage record was matched here (W2 and W10 handle that).
IEM agreement is by Content-Length for most files and by content for four frames; full hash comparison was not run for all files.
The units (mm) and the meanings of codes -1 and -3 are unverified. Inch equivalents assume mm.
The 2-minute bit-depth rule (8 bits when fewer than 128 codes) is an inference from the decoded files.
The NSSL table pages and the GitHub CSV tables were not read in this session.
Downloads: 106284891 bytes of data and document GETs (unique files). S3 listing bytes (42510881 bytes over 206 requests) are reported separately and are not downloads.
'Montana crop' (43.0 to 50.5 N, 118.5 to 101.0 W) is a lat/lon box of 1312500 cells, not the state; it includes parts of Canada and neighbouring states.
The bucket's 2020-10-14 folder holds 112 of about 720 frames; 'no missing days' is true for folders only.
On 2025-06-26 the 1440-minute file is not the maximum of the archived two-minute frames; the cause is not established.
open_questions: What are the MESH units (mm?) and the meanings of codes -1 and -3? The NSSL GRIB2 table (TLS not verifiable here) or the GitHub CSV tables must be read from a session with access.
Why do two-minute bit depths follow the frame maximum (8-bit at 22.5 or less), and does the rule hold in every year?

Which copy is authoritative when the IEM and the NOAA bucket differ at 12:00 UTC (2025-06-26, 2025-06-27, 2026-05-26, 2026-09-11)? On 2025-06-26 the IEM copy is closer to the frame maximum (18571 against 211686 points); neither equals it.
Why does the 1440-minute file differ from the maximum of the archived two-minute frames on 2025-06-26 (721 frames), and does it match on other days? The two researcher days were not re-run.

Are the very large maxima real or artifacts? Candidates: 457.4 near 31.26 N, 88.58 W; 313-unit copy disagreement at 31.265 N, 88.595 W; 199.8 near 52.37 N, 108.84 W in January. W10 needs a plausibility rule.
Does IEM hold the 2021-10-17 to 2022-06-14 1440-minute files under another name, or are they absent? HEAD checks at the 12:00 name return 404.
Does the 2022-06-09 12:00 UTC file exist anywhere? The bucket lacks it and IEM has no file in that absent range; the 11:30 file exists.
What did MRMS v12.1 change for MESH? The NCO and PNS notices list MESH products without describing a change; the SCN 21-17 PDF link returns 404.
Is the 'Version 12.2' label correct? It appears beside SPR on the VLab guide, not MESH; the VLab tables page says V12.1.

review.scope: Refuter pass on W1: re-listed the bucket and IEM mirror (sample days, 62 months of 1440-minute keys); decoded about 780 GRIB2 files (62.4 MB), including the 721 two-minute frames of 2025-06-25/26 with both 12Z copies; re-read terms and documentation pages. NSSL tables not reachable with verified TLS. Not re-run: the 2025-06-14/15 and 2025-06-15/16 equality, IEM coverage beyond sample days, live IEM counts, 2020 IEM decodes.
refuted_claims: The 1440-minute file equals the maximum of the 2-minute frames in [T-24 h, T) as a general rule: contradicted on 2025-06-26 12:00.
'Nearest grid point' to 47.0 N, 109.9 W (6.3 and 38.8): four nodes are equidistant, so no single nearest value exists.
Bit depth follows the number of distinct codes: contradicted by 721 frames (8-bit up to 169 codes; 16-bit as few as 127).
Code -3 share 33.36 to 40.08 percent across decoded files: 33.68 to 77.93 percent over 721 frames of one day.
typeOfStatisticalProcessing 'is not returned (None)': pygrib raises a key-not-found error.
corrections: 'Montana crop' is a lat/lon box (1312500 cells), not Montana; its numbers reproduce on 2025-06-16 12:00.
Benchland 'nearest' values are four equidistant nodes (0.673 km each): 2025-06-15 12Z 38.8, 55.1, 45.7, 58.2; 2025-06-16 12Z 6.3, 7.9, 7.8, 9.9.
Grid maximum 108.4 is 23.1 km from 47.0 N, 109.9 W.

Bit-depth rule: the code-count rule is replaced by the scaled-range rule (8-bit when (max - min) / 0.1 is at most 255, grid minimum -3); it fits all 721 frames of 2025-06-25/26 and the 8 frames checked.
'Exact on two days' concerns two days the reviewer did not re-run; 2025-06-26, the first day the reviewer tested, is not exact.
All four size-differing 12Z pairs differ in content (230119, 74514, 35737 and 60500 points); the file checked two.
Medians of even counts end in .5 (for example 2023-06-15 MESH_00.50 53296.5, not 53296).
The 2020-10-14 bucket holds 112 frames (73088 s gap); IEM has about 720. 'No missing days' holds for folders, not frames.
The 45-file day in the 12Z window is 2026-10-07; the 46-file day is 2022-06-09.
'Version 12.2' is beside SPR, not MESH, on the VLab products guide; the VLab MRMS page says 'updated for V12.1'.
SCN 21-17 is effective February 23, 2021 (VLab MRMS page); PNS 20-86 is dated November 19, 2020.
